court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
case_name: Mr. Anvesh Srivastava And Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt.

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt. Govt. Of U.P. Lko And Others

facts_of_case: Petitioners filed writ petitions seeking quashing of FIR and direction not to arrest them. Marriage between petitioner No.1 and opposite party No.5 was solemnized, but soon a dispute arose and an F.I.R. was lodged.

legal_principles.principle: Courts have inherent jurisdiction to pass a suitable order to prevent abuse of process of law and secure the ends of justice.
legal_principles.held: Since both the parties to the matrimonial dispute have arrived at a compromise, in such a situation, the Court has inherent jurisdiction to pass a suitable order as may be necessary to prevent the abuse of process of law to secure the ends of justice.
cited_cases: B.S. Joshi and others vs. State of Haryana and others, (Year) X SCC Y
G.V. Rao v. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors., [(2000) 3 SCC 693]

legal_principles.principle: Courts should encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes.
legal_principles.held: It becomes the duty of the Court to encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes.
cited_cases: B.S. Joshi and others vs. State of Haryana and others, (Year) X SCC Y
G.V. Rao v. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors., [(2000) 3 SCC 693]

outcome.final_order: The impugned First Information Report is quashed, and the petitioners are directed not to be arrested on the basis of the said FIR.

use_for_drafting: representing in Hindu Marriage Act cases
